47	failure; wrong argument counts and a `POSITION` or `QUOTA` that is not an
48	integer print usage on stderr and exit 2.
49	
50	## Public interface
51	
52	`weighted_batcher.Sampler(weights, replacement=True, seed=None)`.
53	- `Sampler.sample(n) -> list[int]` returns drawn indices.
54	- In without-replacement mode draws accumulate on the instance: repeated
55	  `sample` calls never return an index already drawn, and requesting more
56	  draws than the remaining positive-weight items raises `ValueError`.
57	- `Sampler.weights -> list[float]` as supplied.
58	- `weighted_batcher.render_metrics(metrics) -> str` returns one line of JSON.
59	- `weighted_batcher.parse_metrics(line) -> dict` accepts what `render_metrics` produced.
60	- `weighted_batcher.append_metrics(path, line) -> None` validates one JSON object
61	  line and appends it to `path`. Concurrent processes appending to the same file
62	  never interleave records. Raises `OSError` if `line` is not a string or the
63	  path is not writable, `ValueError` if the top level is not a JSON object, and
64	  `TypeError` if a key is not a string or a value is not an int or float
65	  (booleans do not count).
66	- `weighted_batcher.recover_metrics(path) -> list[dict]` reads the log set
67	  back: segments `path.1`, `path.2`, ... in ascending order followed by the
68	  current log at `path`. Every complete newline-terminated line is parsed; a
69	  torn unterminated tail left by a crashed writer is silently discarded.
70	  Blank lines (`\n` and `\r\n`) are skipped. A non-JSON complete line raises
71	  `ValueError` naming its file and line number. An empty or newline-only file
72	  yields `[]`. Missing files raise `FileNotFoundError` (only when neither the
73	  current log nor any segment exists); directories raise
74	  `IsADirectoryError`. Large counters return as exact ints, `-0.0` is
75	  preserved, and key order follows the file.
76	- `weighted_batcher.rotate_metrics(path) -> None` seals the current log into
77	  the next numbered segment (`path.1`, then one past the greatest number
78	  already present, so a deleted number is never reused) and leaves an empty
79	  file at `path`; an empty log seals an empty segment. Concurrent appenders
80	  are serialised with a file lock, so every accepted record lands in exactly
81	  one segment or in the current log. A crash after sealing but before
82	  re-creation still leaves the segment readable in write order. Raises
83	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
84	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking failure.
85	- `weighted_batcher.iter_metrics(path)` is the streaming counterpart of
86	  `recover_metrics`: it yields records line by line across segments and the
87	  current log without loading them into memory, with the same parsing and
88	  error semantics.
89	- `weighted_batcher.compact_metrics(path) -> None` merges all segments and
90	  the current log into the single fixed segment `path.1` and leaves the
91	  current log empty; a completely empty set still yields an empty segment.
92	  Complete records are copied byte for byte with their original newlines —
93	  not re-rendered, de-duplicated or reordered, so `-0.0`, oversized counters
94	  and key order are preserved; torn tails are dropped and blank lines
95	  skipped just like on read. The merge is fully written and flushed to a
96	  temporary file before being atomically published as `path.compact`, and
97	  only then are old segments removed and the result renamed to `path.1`;
98	  a half-written crash leftover never joins recovery, and while staging
99	  exists recovery and streaming read only it. A later append, rotation or
100	  compaction transparently finishes an interrupted cleanup. Raises
101	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
102	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write failure.
103	- `weighted_batcher.resume_metrics(path, position=0)` streams records from
104	  `position` onward, where `position` is the number of records already read
105	  from the start of the segment set in write order. The position needs no
106	  conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
107	  cleanup, and is only out of range when it exceeds the record total
108	  (pruned records included); equal to the total the stream is empty.
109	  Reading stays line by line and linear, never materialising the segment
110	  set. Raises `TypeError` if `position` is not an integer (booleans do not
111	  count), `ValueError` for a negative or out-of-range position (the latter
112	  while iterating), with the same path and line-level errors as
113	  `iter_metrics`.
114	- `weighted_batcher.prune_metrics(path, quota)` keeps at most `quota`
115	  records, dropping whole records from the oldest end in write order;
116	  `quota` 0 drops every record, and a quota at or above the current count
117	  removes nothing. A record is never split, empty and torn-tail-only
118	  segments spend no quota, and survivors keep their bytes, order,
119	  newlines, `-0.0`, oversized counters and key order. The set remembers
120	  the number of records pruned (`path.prune`), so pruned records keep
121	  their write-order ordinals for `resume_metrics`. Whole evicted segments
122	  are deleted and only the single boundary segment is rewritten, staged
123	  atomically at `path.trim`; a crash leaves either the old set or a set
124	  pruned to a complete record boundary, and a half-finished trim never
125	  joins recovery. Pruning is serialised with appends, rotations and
126	  compactions, and an unfinished compaction is settled first. Raises
127	  `TypeError` if `quota` is not an integer (booleans do not count),
128	  `ValueError` for a negative quota, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is
129	  missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a
130	  non-string path or a locking/write failure. Old segment sets with no
131	  prune marker need no migration; the first prune starts at zero pruned.
132	- `weighted_batcher.snapshot_metrics(path) -> str` pins the complete
133	  record sequence as of the call and returns a persistable snapshot
134	  handle. The pinned records are copied byte for byte into a
135	  snapshot-private file, so no later append, rotation, compaction or
136	  prune changes what the snapshot reads — the records survive even a
137	  quota-0 prune, and a compaction rewriting the segment members leaves
138	  the creation-time bytes (original newlines, `-0.0`, oversized
139	  counters, key order) untouched. Snapshots are independent of each
140	  other. A crash mid-creation leaves no usable handle behind, and the
141	  orphaned copy is removed transparently by the next write. Raises
142	  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
143	  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write
144	  failure.
145	- `weighted_batcher.release_metrics(path, handle) -> None` releases a
146	  snapshot handle and deletes its private copy. Reading or releasing the
147	  handle afterwards raises `ValueError`, as does a forged handle or one
148	  belonging to another segment set. Raises `TypeError` if `handle` is
149	  not a string, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing,
150	  `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a non-string
151	  path or a locking/write failure.
152	- `weighted_batcher.resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position=0)`
153	  streams the records pinned for `handle` from `position` onward, with
154	  the same write-order ordinals as `resume_metrics`: records pruned
155	  before the snapshot still occupy their ordinals, a position inside
156	  that pruned region starts at the oldest record the snapshot holds, and
157	  only a position past the creation-time record total (pruned included)
158	  is out of range — equal to the total the stream is empty. Repeated
159	  reads of the same handle always yield the creation-time slice, and
160	  reading never touches the segment-set members, so a member pruned or
161	  compacted away concurrently raises no `FileNotFoundError`. Raises
162	  `TypeError` if `handle` is not a string or `position` is not an
163	  integer (booleans do not count), `ValueError` for a forged, foreign or
164	  released handle and for a negative or out-of-range position (the
165	  latter while iterating), `FileNotFoundError` when neither the log nor
166	  any segment exists, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError`
167	  for a non-string path.
168	
169	## Tests
170	
171	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
172	
173	## Limits
174	
175	The sampler is single-threaded and deterministic per seed.
176	Counters are integers; no floating point rounding is applied to them.
177	No dataset loading and no training loop.

# weighted-batcher

Weighted sampling helpers whose selection sequence is reproducible from a seed, plus metric rendering that keeps very large counters exact.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m weighted_batcher --selftest

Append one metric line to a durable log, recover the log back as JSON, seal it into a numbered segment, stream it back, compact every segment into one, or resume reading at a saved position:

    python3 -m weighted_batcher record FILE METRICS_JSON
    python3 -m weighted_batcher recover FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher rotate FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher stream FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher compact FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher resume FILE [POSITION]
    python3 -m weighted_batcher prune FILE QUOTA
    python3 -m weighted_batcher snapshot FILE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher release FILE HANDLE
    python3 -m weighted_batcher snap-resume FILE HANDLE [POSITION]

`recover` and `stream` print one JSON object per line on stdout and exit 0.
`rotate` seals `FILE` into a numbered segment (`FILE.1`, then one past the
highest number already present), leaving an empty `FILE` behind, and exits 0.
`compact` merges every segment and the current log into `FILE.1`, leaving an
empty `FILE` behind; an empty log set still produces an empty `FILE.1`.
`resume` prints records from `POSITION` (the number of records already read
from the start in write order, default 0) onward; the position stays valid
across appends, rotations, compactions and pruning. `prune` retains at most
`QUOTA` records, dropping the oldest whole records; `QUOTA` 0 drops every
record. Pruned records keep their write-order positions, so a `POSITION`
inside or at the prune point reads from the oldest surviving record, and
only a position past the total record count (pruned included) is out of
range. `snapshot` pins the complete record sequence at creation time and
prints a persistable handle; `snap-resume` streams the pinned sequence
from `POSITION` (same ordinal rules as `resume`, default 0), and
`release` retires the handle. `rotate`, `stream`, `compact`, `resume`,
`prune`, `snapshot`, `release` and `snap-resume` exit 1 on
failure; wrong argument counts and a `POSITION` or `QUOTA` that is not an
integer print usage on stderr and exit 2.

## Public interface

`weighted_batcher.Sampler(weights, replacement=True, seed=None)`.
- `Sampler.sample(n) -> list[int]` returns drawn indices.
- In without-replacement mode draws accumulate on the instance: repeated
  `sample` calls never return an index already drawn, and requesting more
  draws than the remaining positive-weight items raises `ValueError`.
- `Sampler.weights -> list[float]` as supplied.
- `weighted_batcher.render_metrics(metrics) -> str` returns one line of JSON.
- `weighted_batcher.parse_metrics(line) -> dict` accepts what `render_metrics` produced.
- `weighted_batcher.append_metrics(path, line) -> None` validates one JSON object
  line and appends it to `path`. Concurrent processes appending to the same file
  never interleave records. Raises `OSError` if `line` is not a string or the
  path is not writable, `ValueError` if the top level is not a JSON object, and
  `TypeError` if a key is not a string or a value is not an int or float
  (booleans do not count).
- `weighted_batcher.recover_metrics(path) -> list[dict]` reads the log set
  back: segments `path.1`, `path.2`, ... in ascending order followed by the
  current log at `path`. Every complete newline-terminated line is parsed; a
  torn unterminated tail left by a crashed writer is silently discarded.
  Blank lines (`\n` and `\r\n`) are skipped. A non-JSON complete line raises
  `ValueError` naming its file and line number. An empty or newline-only file
  yields `[]`. Missing files raise `FileNotFoundError` (only when neither the
  current log nor any segment exists); directories raise
  `IsADirectoryError`. Large counters return as exact ints, `-0.0` is
  preserved, and key order follows the file.
- `weighted_batcher.rotate_metrics(path) -> None` seals the current log into
  the next numbered segment (`path.1`, then one past the greatest number
  already present, so a deleted number is never reused) and leaves an empty
  file at `path`; an empty log seals an empty segment. Concurrent appenders
  are serialised with a file lock, so every accepted record lands in exactly
  one segment or in the current log. A crash after sealing but before
  re-creation still leaves the segment readable in write order. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking failure.
- `weighted_batcher.iter_metrics(path)` is the streaming counterpart of
  `recover_metrics`: it yields records line by line across segments and the
  current log without loading them into memory, with the same parsing and
  error semantics.
- `weighted_batcher.compact_metrics(path) -> None` merges all segments and
  the current log into the single fixed segment `path.1` and leaves the
  current log empty; a completely empty set still yields an empty segment.
  Complete records are copied byte for byte with their original newlines —
  not re-rendered, de-duplicated or reordered, so `-0.0`, oversized counters
  and key order are preserved; torn tails are dropped and blank lines
  skipped just like on read. The merge is fully written and flushed to a
  temporary file before being atomically published as `path.compact`, and
  only then are old segments removed and the result renamed to `path.1`;
  a half-written crash leftover never joins recovery, and while staging
  exists recovery and streaming read only it. A later append, rotation or
  compaction transparently finishes an interrupted cleanup. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_metrics(path, position=0)` streams records from
  `position` onward, where `position` is the number of records already read
  from the start of the segment set in write order. The position needs no
  conversion across appends, rotations, compactions, prunes or crash
  cleanup, and is only out of range when it exceeds the record total
  (pruned records included); equal to the total the stream is empty.
  Reading stays line by line and linear, never materialising the segment
  set. Raises `TypeError` if `position` is not an integer (booleans do not
  count), `ValueError` for a negative or out-of-range position (the latter
  while iterating), with the same path and line-level errors as
  `iter_metrics`.
- `weighted_batcher.prune_metrics(path, quota)` keeps at most `quota`
  records, dropping whole records from the oldest end in write order;
  `quota` 0 drops every record, and a quota at or above the current count
  removes nothing. A record is never split, empty and torn-tail-only
  segments spend no quota, and survivors keep their bytes, order,
  newlines, `-0.0`, oversized counters and key order. The set remembers
  the number of records pruned (`path.prune`), so pruned records keep
  their write-order ordinals for `resume_metrics`. Whole evicted segments
  are deleted and only the single boundary segment is rewritten, staged
  atomically at `path.trim`; a crash leaves either the old set or a set
  pruned to a complete record boundary, and a half-finished trim never
  joins recovery. Pruning is serialised with appends, rotations and
  compactions, and an unfinished compaction is settled first. Raises
  `TypeError` if `quota` is not an integer (booleans do not count),
  `ValueError` for a negative quota, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is
  missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a
  non-string path or a locking/write failure. Old segment sets with no
  prune marker need no migration; the first prune starts at zero pruned.
- `weighted_batcher.snapshot_metrics(path) -> str` pins the complete
  record sequence as of the call and returns a persistable snapshot
  handle. The pinned records are copied byte for byte into a
  snapshot-private file, so no later append, rotation, compaction or
  prune changes what the snapshot reads — the records survive even a
  quota-0 prune, and a compaction rewriting the segment members leaves
  the creation-time bytes (original newlines, `-0.0`, oversized
  counters, key order) untouched. Snapshots are independent of each
  other. A crash mid-creation leaves no usable handle behind, and the
  orphaned copy is removed transparently by the next write. Raises
  `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing, `IsADirectoryError` for a
  directory, and `OSError` for a non-string path or a locking/write
  failure.
- `weighted_batcher.release_metrics(path, handle) -> None` releases a
  snapshot handle and deletes its private copy. Reading or releasing the
  handle afterwards raises `ValueError`, as does a forged handle or one
  belonging to another segment set. Raises `TypeError` if `handle` is
  not a string, `FileNotFoundError` if the log is missing,
  `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError` for a non-string
  path or a locking/write failure.
- `weighted_batcher.resume_snapshot_metrics(path, handle, position=0)`
  streams the records pinned for `handle` from `position` onward, with
  the same write-order ordinals as `resume_metrics`: records pruned
  before the snapshot still occupy their ordinals, a position inside
  that pruned region starts at the oldest record the snapshot holds, and
  only a position past the creation-time record total (pruned included)
  is out of range — equal to the total the stream is empty. Repeated
  reads of the same handle always yield the creation-time slice, and
  reading never touches the segment-set members, so a member pruned or
  compacted away concurrently raises no `FileNotFoundError`. Raises
  `TypeError` if `handle` is not a string or `position` is not an
  integer (booleans do not count), `ValueError` for a forged, foreign or
  released handle and for a negative or out-of-range position (the
  latter while iterating), `FileNotFoundError` when neither the log nor
  any segment exists, `IsADirectoryError` for a directory, and `OSError`
  for a non-string path.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

The sampler is single-threaded and deterministic per seed.
Counters are integers; no floating point rounding is applied to them.
No dataset loading and no training loop.

1	"""Weighted sampling helpers and exact metric serialisation."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import bisect
6	import json
7	import math
8	import numbers
9	import random
10	
11	__all__ = [
12	    "Sampler",
13	    "render_metrics",
14	    "parse_metrics",
15	    "append_metrics",
16	    "recover_metrics",
17	    "rotate_metrics",
18	    "iter_metrics",
19	    "compact_metrics",
20	    "resume_metrics",
21	    "prune_metrics",
22	    "snapshot_metrics",
23	    "release_metrics",
24	    "resume_snapshot_metrics",
25	    "snapshot_diff_metrics",
26	    "resume_snapshot_delta_metrics",
27	]
28	
29	
30	class Sampler:
31	    """Draw indices with probability proportional to their effective weight.
32	
33	    The effective weight of ``0`` and ``-0.0`` is zero: such items can never
34	    be drawn.  All draws from one instance share a single PRNG stream, so the
35	    sequence produced from a given ``seed`` is reproducible item by item.
36	
37	    Without replacement, draws accumulate across calls: an index drawn by
38	    one :meth:`sample` call is never drawn again by a later call on the same
39	    instance, and requesting more draws than the remaining positive-weight
40	    items raises :class:`ValueError`.
41	    """
42	
43	    def __init__(self, weights, replacement=True, seed=None):
44	        checked = []
45	        for w in weights:
46	            if isinstance(w, bool) or not isinstance(w, numbers.Real):
47	                raise TypeError(
48	                    f"weight must be a real number, got {type(w).__name__}"
49	                )
50	            if math.isnan(w) or math.isinf(w):
51	                raise ValueError("weight must not be NaN or Infinity")
52	            if w < 0:
53	                raise ValueError("weight must not be negative")
54	            checked.append(w)
55	        self._weights = checked
56	        self._replacement = bool(replacement)
57	        self._rng = random.Random(seed)
58	        # Effective weights as floats; 0 and -0.0 both collapse to zero.
59	        self._effective = [float(w) if w > 0 else 0.0 for w in checked]
60	        self._positive = sum(1 for e in self._effective if e > 0.0)
61	        cumulative = []
62	        total = 0.0
63	        for e in self._effective:
64	            total += e
65	            cumulative.append(total)
66	        self._cumulative = cumulative
67	        # Without-replacement pool, depleted across repeated sample() calls.
68	        self._remaining = [i for i, e in enumerate(self._effective) if e > 0.0]
69	
70	    @property
71	    def weights(self):
72	        """The weights as supplied to the constructor."""
73	        return list(self._weights)
74	
75	    def sample(self, n):
76	        """Return a list of ``n`` drawn indices."""
77	        if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int):
78	            raise TypeError(f"sample count must be an integer, got {type(n).__name__}")
79	        if n < 0:
80	            raise ValueError("sample count must not be negative")
81	        if n == 0:
82	            return []
83	        if self._replacement:
84	            if self._positive == 0:
85	                raise ValueError("no items with positive weight to draw from")
86	            return self._sample_with_replacement(n)
87	        remaining = len(self._remaining)
88	        if n > remaining:
89	            raise ValueError(
90	                f"cannot draw {n} items without replacement: only "
91	                f"{remaining} positive-weight items remain"
92	            )
93	        return self._sample_without_replacement(n)
94	
95	    def _draw_one(self, cumulative, total):
96	        r = self._rng.random() * total
97	        i = bisect.bisect_right(cumulative, r)
98	        # Guard against r rounding up to exactly total.
99	        return min(i, len(cumulative) - 1)
100	
101	    def _sample_with_replacement(self, n):
102	        total = self._cumulative[-1] if self._cumulative else 0.0
103	        return [self._draw_one(self._cumulative, total) for _ in range(n)]
104	
105	    def _sample_without_replacement(self, n):
106	        # The pool persists on the instance, so draws stay distinct across
107	        # repeated sample() calls.
108	        drawn = []
109	        for _ in range(n):
110	            total = 0.0
111	            cumulative = []
112	            for i in self._remaining:
113	                total += self._effective[i]
114	                cumulative.append(total)
115	            pos = self._draw_one(cumulative, total)
116	            drawn.append(self._remaining.pop(pos))
117	        return drawn
118	
119	
120	def render_metrics(metrics):
121	    """Render a name-to-number mapping as one compact JSON line.
122	
123	    Keys keep their insertion order.  Integers are written as exact decimal
124	    integers regardless of magnitude; the line ends with a single newline.
125	    """
126	    for key, value in metrics.items():
127	        if not isinstance(key, str):
128	            raise TypeError(f"metric name must be a string, got {type(key).__name__}")
129	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
130	            raise TypeError(
131	                f"metric value must be an int or float, got {type(value).__name__}"
132	            )
133	        if isinstance(value, float) and (math.isnan(value) or math.isinf(value)):
134	            raise ValueError("metric value must not be NaN or Infinity")
135	    return json.dumps(metrics, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
136	
137	
138	def parse_metrics(line):
139	    """Parse a line produced by :func:`render_metrics` back into a dict."""
140	    if not isinstance(line, str):
141	        raise TypeError(f"expected a string, got {type(line).__name__}")
142	
143	    def _reject_constant(name):
144	        raise ValueError(f"invalid numeric constant {name}")
145	
146	    try:
147	        data = json.loads(line, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
148	    except ValueError as exc:
149	        raise ValueError(f"invalid metrics line: {exc}") from exc
150	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
151	        raise ValueError("metrics line must be a JSON object at the top level")
152	    return data
153	
154	
155	from .persistence import (  # noqa: E402
156	    append_metrics,
157	    compact_metrics,
158	    iter_metrics,
159	    prune_metrics,
160	    recover_metrics,
161	    release_metrics,
162	    resume_metrics,
163	    resume_snapshot_delta_metrics,
164	    resume_snapshot_metrics,
165	    rotate_metrics,
166	    snapshot_diff_metrics,
167	    snapshot_metrics,
168	)

    The effective weight of ``0`` and ``-0.0`` is zero: such items can never
    be drawn.  All draws from one instance share a single PRNG stream, so the
    sequence produced from a given ``seed`` is reproducible item by item.

    Without replacement, draws accumulate across calls: an index drawn by
    one :meth:`sample` call is never drawn again by a later call on the same
    instance, and requesting more draws than the remaining positive-weight
    items raises :class:`ValueError`.
    """

    def __init__(self, weights, replacement=True, seed=None):
        checked = []
        for w in weights:
            if isinstance(w, bool) or not isinstance(w, numbers.Real):
                raise TypeError(
                    f"weight must be a real number, got {type(w).__name__}"
                )
            if math.isnan(w) or math.isinf(w):
                raise ValueError("weight must not be NaN or Infinity")
            if w < 0:
                raise ValueError("weight must not be negative")
            checked.append(w)
        self._weights = checked
        self._replacement = bool(replacement)
        self._rng = random.Random(seed)
        # Effective weights as floats; 0 and -0.0 both collapse to zero.
        self._effective = [float(w) if w > 0 else 0.0 for w in checked]
        self._positive = sum(1 for e in self._effective if e > 0.0)
        cumulative = []
        total = 0.0
        for e in self._effective:
            total += e
            cumulative.append(total)
        self._cumulative = cumulative
        # Without-replacement pool, depleted across repeated sample() calls.
        self._remaining = [i for i, e in enumerate(self._effective) if e > 0.0]

    @property
    def weights(self):
        """The weights as supplied to the constructor."""
        return list(self._weights)

    def sample(self, n):
        """Return a list of ``n`` drawn indices."""
        if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int):
            raise TypeError(f"sample count must be an integer, got {type(n).__name__}")
        if n < 0:
            raise ValueError("sample count must not be negative")
        if n == 0:
            return []
        if self._replacement:
            if self._positive == 0:
                raise ValueError("no items with positive weight to draw from")
            return self._sample_with_replacement(n)
        remaining = len(self._remaining)
        if n > remaining:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cannot draw {n} items without replacement: only "
                f"{remaining} positive-weight items remain"
            )
        return self._sample_without_replacement(n)

    def _draw_one(self, cumulative, total):
        r = self._rng.random() * total
        i = bisect.bisect_right(cumulative, r)
        # Guard against r rounding up to exactly total.
        return min(i, len(cumulative) - 1)

    def _sample_with_replacement(self, n):
        total = self._cumulative[-1] if self._cumulative else 0.0
        return [self._draw_one(self._cumulative, total) for _ in range(n)]

    def _sample_without_replacement(self, n):
        # The pool persists on the instance, so draws stay distinct across
        # repeated sample() calls.
        drawn = []
        for _ in range(n):
            total = 0.0
            cumulative = []
            for i in self._remaining:
                total += self._effective[i]
                cumulative.append(total)
            pos = self._draw_one(cumulative, total)
            drawn.append(self._remaining.pop(pos))
        return drawn


def render_metrics(metrics):
    """Render a name-to-number mapping as one compact JSON line.

    Keys keep their insertion order.  Integers are written as exact decimal
    integers regardless of magnitude; the line ends with a single newline.
    """
    for key, value in metrics.items():
        if not isinstance(key, str):
            raise TypeError(f"metric name must be a string, got {type(key).__name__}")
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise TypeError(
                f"metric value must be an int or float, got {type(value).__name__}"
            )
        if isinstance(value, float) and (math.isnan(value) or math.isinf(value)):
            raise ValueError("metric value must not be NaN or Infinity")
    return json.dumps(metrics, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"


def parse_metrics(line):
    """Parse a line produced by :func:`render_metrics` back into a dict."""
    if not isinstance(line, str):
        raise TypeError(f"expected a string, got {type(line).__name__}")

    def _reject_constant(name):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid numeric constant {name}")

    try:
        data = json.loads(line, parse_constant=_reject_constant)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"invalid metrics line: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError("metrics line must be a JSON object at the top level")
    return data


from .persistence import (  # noqa: E402
    append_metrics,
    compact_metrics,
    iter_metrics,
    prune_metrics,
    recover_metrics,
    release_metrics,
    resume_metrics,
    resume_snapshot_delta_metrics,
    resume_snapshot_metrics,
    rotate_metrics,
    snapshot_diff_metrics,
    snapshot_metrics,
)

1	"""Durable append-only metric log with rotation, compaction, pruning and resume.
2	
3	Each metric occupies exactly one newline-terminated JSON line.  A record is
4	appended with :func:`os.write` against a single ``O_APPEND`` file
5	descriptor, so concurrent appending processes never interleave one line
6	with another.  Recovery acknowledges only newline-terminated lines: a
7	record torn by a mid-write crash survives as an unterminated tail and is
8	silently discarded.
9	
10	:func:`rotate_metrics` seals the current log into a numbered segment
11	(``path.1``, ``path.2``, ...) and leaves an empty log behind.  Segment
12	numbers are one past the highest number ever used, so deleting a segment
13	from the outside never makes its number come back.  Recovery walks the
14	segments in ascending order followed by the current log, so a record
15	accepted before a rotation never crosses a segment boundary.
16	:func:`iter_metrics` performs the same walk as a line-by-line generator,
17	never loading the segment set into memory.
18	
19	:func:`compact_metrics` merges every segment and the current log into the
20	single fixed segment ``path.1`` and leaves an empty current log.  Records
21	are copied byte for byte, still newline terminated, without re-rendering.
22	The merge lands first in a staging file at ``path.compact``; only after it
23	is fully on disk does cleanup begin.
24	
25	:func:`prune_metrics` enforces a retention quota by dropping whole records
26	from the oldest end.  Evicted records keep their write-order ordinal: the
27	segment set remembers how many records have been pruned in ``path.prune``,
28	and no operation renumbers surviving records.  :func:`resume_metrics`
29	resumes the same write-order walk at an integer read position; the
30	position needs no translation across appends, rotations, compactions,
31	pruning or crash cleanup.
32	
33	:func:`snapshot_metrics` pins the complete record sequence at creation
34	time into a snapshot-private copy (``path.snap.<handle>``) and records the
35	handle in the snapshot registry (``path.snapshots``), so later appends,
36	rotations, compactions and prunes never change what the snapshot reads.
37	:func:`resume_snapshot_metrics` streams a snapshot from a write-order
38	read position with the same ordinal rules as :func:`resume_metrics`, and
39	:func:`release_metrics` retires a handle and its private copy.  A copy
40	left behind by a crash before its handle was registered is not readable
41	and is removed transparently by the next write.
42	
43	:func:`snapshot_diff_metrics` reconciles two snapshots of one segment set
44	in write order -- the handle created first is the old side -- reporting
45	each extra record as ``added``, each vanished one as ``missing`` and each
46	byte-for-byte changed one as ``changed``, one JSON line per difference.
47	:func:`resume_snapshot_delta_metrics` pins the live record boundary the
48	way :func:`snapshot_metrics` pins a snapshot (a brief lock to settle and
49	capture the members, then a lock-free copy) and streams the records past
50	a read position that the holder of an older snapshot handle has not read
51	yet.  A reconciliation is fully lock free, and an incremental pull holds
52	the write lock only for the constant-sized boundary pin -- never while
53	its records are produced -- so appends, rotations, compactions and
54	prunes proceed normally while either read runs.
55	
56	Every data-file descriptor is released before a rename on platforms that
57	cannot rename open files (Windows), so sealing, compaction and pruning no
58	longer raise ``PermissionError`` there.

456	    resolves again.  Pruning commits in the order plan publication,
457	    filesystem cleanup, marker finalisation, so an unchanged marker
458	    brackets a directory state that marker reconciles to exactly one
459	    settled record sequence:
460	
461	    * A compaction's fully landed ``path.compact`` staging file, while
462	      present, alone is the segment set.
463	    * A pending prune plan: evicted members still on disk are ignored,
464	      and while the trimmed boundary waits at ``path.trim`` it stands in
465	      for the boundary member; once the boundary is published its staging
466	      name is gone and the finished member is read directly.
467	    """
468	    members = pruned = None
469	    before = _marker_observation(path)
470	    for _ in range(1000):
471	        members, pruned, after = _resolve_once(path, before)
472	        if after == before:
473	            return members, pruned
474	        before = after
475	    # Extremely contended: return the last self-consistent pair rather
476	    # than loop forever; the data it reads is itself whole.
477	    return members, pruned

480	def _resolve_once(path, marker_raw):
481	    """Resolve one directory state, returning it with the post-listing marker."""
482	    if marker_raw:
483	        data = json.loads(marker_raw.decode("utf-8"))
484	        pruned, plan = (
485	            (int(data["pruned"]), data) if isinstance(data, dict)
486	            else (int(data), None)
487	        )
488	    else:
489	        pruned, plan = 0, None
490	
491	    staging = _staging_path(path)
492	    if os.path.exists(staging):
493	        members = [staging]
494	    elif plan is None:
495	        members = [
496	            f"{path}.{number}" for number in sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
497	        ]
498	        if os.path.exists(path):
499	            members.append(path)
500	    else:
501	        evict = set(plan.get("evict", ()))
502	        target = plan.get("trim")
503	        trim = path + _TRIM_SUFFIX
504	        use_trim = target is not None and os.path.exists(trim)
505	        labels = sorted(_segment_numbers(path))
506	        # Include the live log when it exists, and also when a quota-zero
507	        # cleanup is an instant away from replacing it from its published
508	        # trim, so the committed (empty) set never momentarily vanishes.
509	        if os.path.exists(path) or (use_trim and target == _LIVE_LABEL):
510	            labels.append(_LIVE_LABEL)

513	            if label in evict:
514	                continue

518	                members.append(_label_member(label, path))

520	    return members, pruned, _marker_observation(path)

523	def _iter_lines(path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
524	    """Yield ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` for complete lines in one file.
525	
526	    Reading happens one fixed-size chunk at a time, so an arbitrarily long
527	    single line is streamed rather than requiring the whole file in
528	    memory (only that one line is ever held at once).  The final
529	    unterminated tail is a possible torn write and is never produced, so
530	    callers cannot mistake it for a complete line.
531	    """
532	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY)
533	    pending = b""
534	    lineno = 0
535	    try:
536	        while True:
537	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
538	            if not chunk:
539	                break
540	            pending += chunk
541	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
542	            for raw in complete:
543	                lineno += 1
544	                yield lineno, raw
545	    finally:
546	        os.close(fd)

549	def _parse_lined(lines, label):
550	    """Parse ``(line_number, raw_bytes)`` complete lines into metrics."""
551	    for lineno, raw in lines:
552	        if not raw or raw == b"\r":
553	            # A bare newline or a CRLF blank line carries no record.
554	            continue
555	        try:
556	            text = raw.decode("utf-8")
557	            yield parse_metrics(text)
558	        except ValueError as exc:
559	            raise ValueError(
560	                f"invalid metrics in {label} at line {lineno}: {exc}"
561	            ) from exc

569	def iter_metrics(path):
570	    """Yield metric records across the segments and the current log.
571	
572	    Segments ``path.1``, ``path.2``, ... are streamed first in ascending
573	    segment order, followed by the current log at ``path``.  Files are
574	    read line by line, so the segment set is never loaded into memory and
575	    a single line may be arbitrarily long.

578	    but has not finished cleanup, that staging file alone is read; a
579	    staging file left behind by a crashed compaction is ignored until
580	    another append, rotation or compaction finishes it.  A pending prune
581	    is reconciled the same way: only surviving records are yielded.
582

584	    a segment holding only a torn tail yields nothing.  Blank empty lines
585	    (``\\n``) and CRLF blank lines (``\\r\\n``) are skipped.  Any other
586	    complete line that is not a metrics JSON object raises
587	    :class:`ValueError` naming the file and its 1-based line number.
588	
589	    Path-level problems are reported when this function is called; line
590	    content problems are reported lazily as the offending line is reached.
591	
592	    Raises:
593	        FileNotFoundError: neither ``path`` nor any segment exists.
594	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
595	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string.
596	        ValueError: a non-empty complete line is not a metrics JSON
597	            object (raised while iterating).
598	    """
599	    if not isinstance(path, str):
600	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")

605	    if not members:
606	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no metrics log or segments at {path!r}")

608	    def _generate():
609	        for member in members:
610	            yield from _parse_file(member, member)

612	    return _generate()

630	def _iter_raw_file_records(copy_path, chunksize=_READ_CHUNK):
631	    """Yield each complete record line's raw bytes with its newline.
632	
633	    The chunked walk mirrors :func:`_iter_lines`, but lines are never
634	    parsed or re-rendered: blank lines are skipped exactly as on read,
635	    the torn unterminated tail is dropped, and every other complete line
636	    comes back verbatim with ``\\n`` reattached, so byte-level content
637	    such as ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering survives untouched.
638	    """
639	    fd = os.open(copy_path, os.O_RDONLY)
640	    pending = b""
641	    try:
642	        while True:
643	            chunk = os.read(fd, chunksize)
644	            if not chunk:
645	                break
646	            pending += chunk
647	            *complete, pending = pending.split(b"\n")
648	            for raw in complete:
649	                if raw and raw != b"\r":
650	                    yield raw + b"\n"
651	    finally:
652	        os.close(fd)

659	    for byte exactly as on a fresh read, so compaction and pruning move
660	    original newlines, ``-0.0``, huge counters and key ordering untouched.
661	    """
662	    yield from _iter_raw_file_records(path, chunksize)

671	    empty file.

679	def _finish_staged_compact(path):
680	    """Finish compaction cleanup when a staging file is present.
681	
682	    Called with the writer lock held, both at the end of
683	    :func:`compact_metrics` and by any append, rotation, compaction or
684	    prune that finds a staging file left by a crashed cleanup.  The
685	    staging file only ever holds a whole fully landed segment, so
686	    finishing is pure filesystem cleanup.
687	
688	    The staging file stays the sole authoritative member (see
689	    :func:`_resolve_members`) until the final step: old numbered
690	    segments are removed and the current log is emptied while reads
691	    still resolve to staging, and only then is staging renamed onto
692	    ``path.1``.  Every involved descriptor is closed first, so no handle
693	    is held across the rename, which therefore also succeeds on Windows.
694	    The rename is atomic, so a crash at any point leaves either staging
695	    alone or the finished set, and the readable record sequence equals
696	    the pre-compaction one item by item.
697	    """
698	    staging = _staging_path(path)
699	    if not os.path.exists(staging):
700	        return
701	    for number in _segment_numbers(path):
702	        os.unlink(f"{path}.{number}")
703	    _truncate_live_log(path)
704	    os.replace(staging, f"{path}.1")

714	def rotate_metrics(path):
715	    """Seal the current log into a numbered segment and start a new one.
716	
717	    The segment is named ``path.N`` with ``N`` one greater than the
718	    greatest number already present (``path.1`` for the first rotation),
719	    so a segment that was deleted from the outside never hands its number
720	    back out; an empty log seals an empty segment.  Afterwards ``path``
721	    exists again as an empty file ready for appending.  Every record
722	    acknowledged by a write ends up either wholly in a segment or wholly
723	    in the current log, never split across two.
724	
725	    A crash after the rename but before the live file is recreated still
726	    leaves the sealed segment readable; the next appender recreates the
727	    live log.
728	
729	    Raises:
730	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
731	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
732	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, locking fails, or another OS
733	            error occurs while sealing.  Nothing is written when locking
734	            fails.
735	    """
736	    if not isinstance(path, str):
737	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
738	    if os.path.isdir(path):
739	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
740	
741	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
742	    try:
743	        _finish_pending(path)
744	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
745	        used = _segment_numbers(path)
746	        number = (max(used) + 1) if used else 1
747	        segment = f"{path}.{number}"
748	        # POSIX: the rename happens while the lock fd is held (an open
749	        # file may be renamed); the lock makes appenders reopen the path
750	        # before writing.  Windows has no fd in hand at all, so the
751	        # PermissionError an open live log used to cause cannot happen.
752	        os.rename(path, segment)
753	        # Re-create an empty current log without O_TRUNC: an appender that
754	        # won the unlocked rename window on a lock-less platform may have
755	        # landed a record there first, and it belongs in the current log.
756	        new_fd = os.open(
757	            path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
758	        )
759	        os.close(new_fd)
760	    finally:
761	        if fd is not None:
762	            os.close(fd)

765	def append_metrics(path, line):
766	    """Validate one metric line and append it to the log at ``path``.
767	
768	    The line must be a string holding a JSON object whose values are ints
769	    or floats (booleans are rejected).  It is rendered canonically before
770	    writing, so every call adds exactly one compact newline-terminated
771	    record regardless of the input's spacing.
772	
773	    If another process rotates, compacts or prunes the log while this
774	    call waits for the lock, the descriptor is re-opened against the
775	    settled live file before writing, so no record is misdirected.
776	
777	    Raises:
778	        OSError: ``line`` or ``path`` is not a string, the target cannot
779	            be written, or locking the log fails.  Nothing is written when
780	            locking fails.
781	        ValueError: the line is not valid JSON, its top level is not an
782	            object, or a value is NaN or Infinity.
783	        TypeError: a metric value is neither an int nor a float.
784	    """
785	    if not isinstance(line, str):
786	        raise OSError(
787	            f"metrics line must be a string, got {type(line).__name__}"
788	        )
789	    if not isinstance(path, str):
790	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
791	    metrics = parse_metrics(line)
792	    payload = render_metrics(metrics).encode("utf-8")
793	
794	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=True)
795	    try:
796	        _finish_pending(path)
797	        if fd is None:
798	            # Lock-less platform (Windows): the existence-proving handle is
799	            # already closed and settling ran first, so open a fresh
800	            # O_APPEND descriptor for the write and close it again, leaving
801	            # no handle open across a later rename.
802	            out = os.open(
803	                path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o666
804	            )
805	            try:
806	                _write_bytes(out, payload)
807	            finally:
808	                os.close(out)
809	        else:
810	            # Settling may have replaced the live inode (a crashed
811	            # quota-zero prune); lock the settled file before writing.
812	            fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=True)
813	            # One line per write loop on the locked O_APPEND descriptor:
814	            # the kernel appends each write atomically, so concurrent
815	            # processes do not tear or interleave records.
816	            _write_bytes(fd, payload)
817	    finally:
818	        if fd is not None:
819	            os.close(fd)

822	def compact_metrics(path):
823	    """Merge every segment and the current log into one segment.
824	
825	    All records are copied into the fixed segment ``path.1`` in write
826	    order; the current log is left empty afterwards.  Records move byte
827	    for byte with their original newlines -- nothing is re-rendered,
828	    de-duplicated or reordered, so ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key
829	    order are all preserved.  Residual torn lines are not records and
830	    are dropped; blank lines are skipped as on read; overlong single
831	    lines move as-is.  A completely empty set still produces an empty
832	    ``path.1``.
833	
834	    The merge is first written to a private temporary file and only
835	    renamed onto ``path.compact`` after the whole file has landed and
836	    been flushed (its descriptor already closed, so the rename also
837	    works on Windows), so that name always holds a complete whole
838	    segment: a half-written file left by a crash never joins recovery
839	    and never affects reads.  Once staged, recovery and streaming read
840	    only that segment; cleanup publishes it as ``path.1``, removes the
841	    other numbered segments and empties the current log.  An interrupted
842	    cleanup is finished transparently by the next append, rotation,
843	    compaction or prune.  The pruned-record count stored by earlier
844	    prunes is left untouched.
845	
846	    Raises:
847	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
848	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
849	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing the
850	            merged segment fails.  A failed write removes the private
851	            temporary file and leaves the segment set untouched.
852	    """
853	    if not isinstance(path, str):
854	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
855	    if os.path.isdir(path):
856	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
857	
858	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
859	    try:
860	        # A previous compaction may have staged its segment and died
861	        # before cleanup; settle that world before merging again.  So may
862	        # a previous prune.
863	        _finish_pending(path)
864	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
865	
866	        staging = _staging_path(path)
867	        tmp = staging + ".tmp"
868	        try:
869	            out = os.open(
870	                tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666
871	            )
872	            try:
873	                for member in _segment_members(path):
874	                    for raw in _iter_raw_records(member):
875	                        _write_bytes(out, raw)
876	                os.fsync(out)
877	            finally:
878	                # Closed before the rename: on Windows an open file cannot
879	                # be renamed.
880	                os.close(out)

883	            # segment is the only member reads may use during cleanup.
884	            os.rename(tmp, staging)
885	        except BaseException:
886	            # Nothing reached the staging name: the private temp is the
887	            # only file touched, so removing it leaves the old segments
888	            # and current log exactly as they were.
889	            _unlink_if_exists(tmp)
890	            raise
891	        _finish_staged_compact(path)
892	    finally:
893	        if fd is not None:
894	            os.close(fd)

897	def _stage_trim(path, source, skip):
898	    """Publish the surviving tail of one truncated member at ``path.trim``.
899	
900	    The first ``skip`` complete records of ``source`` are dropped; every
901	    later complete record is copied byte for byte with its original
902	    newline.  Blank lines and the torn unterminated tail are discarded,
903	    matching a read of the truncated segment.  The private temp is fully
904	    written and flushed and its descriptor closed before the atomic
905	    rename, so ``path.trim`` only ever holds a complete whole segment and
906	    the rename works on Windows.
907	    """
908	    tmp = path + _TRIM_TMP_SUFFIX
909	    out = os.open(tmp, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o666)
910	    try:
911	        seen = 0
912	        for raw in _iter_raw_records(source):
913	            if seen < skip:
914	                seen += 1
915	                continue
916	            _write_bytes(out, raw)
917	        os.fsync(out)
918	    finally:
919	        os.close(out)
920	    os.rename(tmp, path + _TRIM_SUFFIX)

923	def prune_metrics(path, quota):
924	    """Retain at most ``quota`` records, dropping the oldest whole records.
925	
926	    ``quota`` is the maximum number of records kept in the segment set;
927	    when it already holds no more than ``quota`` records nothing is
928	    removed, and ``quota`` 0 drops every record.  Records are dropped in
929	    write order from the oldest end, one complete line at a time -- a
930	    record is never split.  Empty segments and segments holding only a
931	    torn tail spend no quota and are removed with the prefix ahead of
932	    them.  Surviving records move byte for byte: order, original
933	    newlines, ``-0.0``, oversized counters and key order are unchanged,
934	    and an overlong single line still counts as exactly one record.
935	
936	    Evicted records keep their write-order ordinals: the set remembers
937	    the total number pruned, so read positions never shift (see
938	    :func:`resume_metrics`).  Whole evicted segments are deleted; only
939	    the single segment the cut lands inside is rewritten, via a
940	    ``path.trim`` staging file and a JSON plan in ``path.prune``, so a
941	    crash leaves either the old set or a set pruned to a complete record
942	    boundary -- a half-finished trim never joins recovery.  Pruning is
943	    serialised with appends, rotations and compactions by the live-log
944	    lock, and an unfinished compaction is settled first; every accepted
945	    record is therefore either kept or dropped, never lost or duplicated.
946	
947	    Raises:
948	        FileNotFoundError: ``path`` does not exist.
949	        IsADirectoryError: ``path`` is a directory.
950	        TypeError: ``quota`` is not an integer (booleans do not count).
951	        ValueError: ``quota`` is negative.
952	        OSError: ``path`` is not a string, or locking or writing the
953	            truncated segment fails.
954	    """
955	    if not isinstance(path, str):
956	        raise OSError(f"log path must be a string, got {type(path).__name__}")
957	    if isinstance(quota, bool) or not isinstance(quota, int):
958	        raise TypeError(
959	            f"retention quota must be an integer, got {type(quota).__name__}"
960	        )
961	    if quota < 0:
962	        raise ValueError("retention quota must not be negative")
963	    if os.path.isdir(path):
964	        raise IsADirectoryError(f"log path is a directory: {path!r}")
965	
966	    fd = _mutation_lock(path, create=False)
967	    try:
968	        _finish_pending(path)
969	        fd = _relock_after_settle(fd, path, create=False)
970	
971	        members = _segment_members(path)
972	        # One streaming count pass (the same cheap line walk reads use)
973	        # locates the cut; only the single boundary member is rewritten.
974	        counts = [sum(1 for _ in _iter_raw_records(member))
975	                  for member in members]
976	        total = sum(counts)
977	        if total <= quota:
978	            return
979	        drop = total - quota
980	
981	        index = 0
982	        cumulative = 0
983	        while index < len(members) and drop >= cumulative + counts[index]:
984	            cumulative += counts[index]
985	            index += 1
986	        if index < len(members):
987	            boundary_index = index
988	            skip = drop - cumulative
989	        else:
990	            # Every record lies inside the dropped prefix.  The live log
991	            # is the last member and always exists, so it is the boundary
992	            # and is rewritten empty; everything before it is deleted.
993	            boundary_index = len(members) - 1
994	            skip = counts[-1]
995	        boundary = members[boundary_index]
996	        evict = [
997	            _member_label(name, path) for name in members[:boundary_index]
998	        ]
999	
1000	        pruned = _read_prune_state(path)[0] + drop
1001	        if skip:
1002	            _stage_trim(path, boundary, skip)
1003	            target = _member_label(boundary, path)
1004	        else:
1005	            # The cut lands exactly on a member boundary: that member is
1006	            # already the oldest survivor and needs no rewrite.
1007	            target = None
1008	        # Publishing the plan is the commit point; from here on readers
1009	        # reconcile to the committed set even if cleanup is interrupted.
1010	        plan = json.dumps(
1011	            {"pruned": pruned, "evict": evict, "trim": target},
1012	            separators=(",", ":"),
1013	        )
1014	        _replace_marker(path, plan)
1015	        _finish_staged_prune(path)
1016	    finally:
1017	        if fd is not None:
1018	            os.close(fd)

1021	def resume_metrics(path, position=0):
1022	    """Stream records starting at integer read position ``position``.

1025	    the ordinals :func:`iter_metrics` walks with pruning applied:
1026	    records pruned from the oldest end keep their ordinals and the set
1027	    remembers how many are gone.  Streaming therefore starts at the
1028	    first surviving record whose ordinal is not less than ``position``;

1422	    released, so an upstream append, rotation, compaction or prune is

1429	      later mutation;

1432	      unnamed from birth, that is immune to truncation and dies with the

1469	    otherwise (the locked retry) the copy is uninterrupted.
